intro.title: forwardRef & Exposing DOM Nodes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form where you can focus a custom input field by clicking a button outside of it. You'll learn how to use the forwardRef pattern in Vue to expose a DOM node from a child component to its parent. This involves using Vue's ref system and the defineExpose macro to make internal elements accessible. By the end, you'll understand how to control DOM elements across component boundaries in a Vue application.
intro.usecase: In Vue applications, exposing DOM nodes with forwardRef is essential when building reusable form components like custom input fields, date pickers, or rich text editors. This pattern allows parent components to directly access child DOM elements to programmatically trigger focus, select text, or measure dimensions—common requirements in data-intensive dashboards and admin panels. For example, in a multi-step registration form, you might use forwardRef to automatically focus the next input field after validation, or in a financial dashboard to scroll a specific data table into view. This technique is also valuable for integrating third-party libraries that require direct DOM manipulation, such as charting tools or drag-and-drop interfaces.
